name: CaMMT
description: Cultural content poses challenges for machine translation systems due to the differences in conceptualizations between cultures, where language alone may fail to convey sufficient context to capture region-specific meanings. In this work, we investigate whether images can act as cultural context in multimodal translation. We introduce CaMMT, a human-curated benchmark of over 5,800 triples of images along with parallel captions in English and regional languages. Using this dataset, we evaluate five Vision Language Models (VLMs) in text-only and text+image settings. Through automatic and human evaluations, we find that visual context generally improves translation quality, especially in handling Culturally-Specific Items (CSIs), disambiguation, and correct gender usage. By releasing CaMMT, we aim to support broader efforts in building and evaluating multimodal translation systems that are better aligned with cultural nuance and regional variation.
reputation: Emerging dataset in the multimodal machine translation community focused on cultural context; useful but not yet widely adopted outside specialized research on culturally-aware MT.
notes: Relatively small (≈5.8k examples) and human-curated; requires human evaluation for cultural correctness. Potential contamination risk if model pretraining included similar parallel captions; not saturated and best evaluated with complementary human judgments.
